findings.title: Fallback locale files are never loaded from I18n.translate
findings.body: translate in lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb only calls load_locale for config.locale (line 68), then either returns translate_no_cache immediately when arguments are present (line 69) or caches that call (line 74). The new FallbackLocaleList#ensure_loaded! is invoked only from ApplicationController#set_locale. Mailers, Sidekiq jobs, rails runner, and any I18n.with_locale / I18n.locale= path never hit that filter, so the lazy loader never reads the site-default or :en YAML. I18n::Backend::Fallbacks then searches empty catalogs and I18n.t becomes "translation missing: ..." for keys that exist only in a fallback locale — the main server-side case this change is for. Because the LRU cache stores that miss under key+locale+backend object id and nothing invalidates it when catalogs are loaded later, a lookup that runs before set_locale (boot, middleware, an earlier before_filter, or another thread) keeps serving the missing string for the life of the cache entry even on later web requests that do call ensure_loaded!.

findings.title: Translation cache key ignores the fallback chain
findings.body: The accelerator cache key is only "#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}" (lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb:72). Resolved strings now depend on SiteSetting.default_locale via FallbackLocaleList#[] and on which fallback catalogs were loaded. default_locale is a runtime admin setting and is not part of the key, and neither ensure_loaded! nor a default-locale change calls I18n.reload! (the only path that nils @cache). After an admin changes the site locale, arg-less I18n.t calls keep returning the previously cached fallback translation until that LRU slot is evicted or the process restarts, so users keep seeing the old language for missing keys.

findings.title: No coverage for fallback order or non-request loading
findings.body: The new fallback chain in config/initializers/i18n.rb (locale, SiteSetting.default_locale, :en) and the lazy-load hook are untested. Nothing asserts that a key missing from the user locale is served from the site locale and then :en, that pluralization still runs on the fallback locale, or that I18n.t falls back when locale is set outside ApplicationController (the mailer/job path). Without that, the broken load/cache behavior above can ship unnoticed, and a later change to FallbackLocaleList or translate_accelerator can drop fallbacks in production only.
